decisions.reason: The black-finish range costs little to keep as a finish variant of existing drains, but it was only mentioned on the website and the design trend may fade, so the option stays open with moderately higher withdrawal risk.
The shower channel for seamless coverings sits close to the core, has its own page and fits the barrier-free bathroom trend, so holding costs are low and its upside is still being realized.
The tileable floor drain is a natural extension of the standard range with minimal incremental cost and steady installer demand, so there is no reason to abandon it.

The pump-drain shower channel was launched only in 2024 and its value is still uncertain, so the option is worth keeping open despite the withdrawal of the earlier pump-assisted line, which signals this segment carries higher risk.
